SMTO-CFG-0010 — The Gateway couldn't start: input wait time can't be negative

GUID: fdf0d782-7205-42ce-aba9-a77b98b8fe3f
Slug: gateway-config-gateway-terminal-input-idle-seconds-must-be
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer, stopped right after starting. Its wait time for spotting a command that needs typed input is below zero. No settings were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, find GATEWAY_TERMINAL_INPUT_IDLE_SECONDS in the command or settings used to start it. This setting holds the negative value the Gateway refused.
  2. Set it to 15 (the normal value), to another number of seconds, or to 0 to turn this check off. You can also remove it to use the normal value. A waiting time can't be less than zero, while 0 or more seconds is accepted.
  3. Start the Gateway again. Then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on that Gateway. This shows whether the Gateway now starts with the corrected value and SMTO can reach it.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway keeps running after it starts, and in Settings › Setup › Gateways it shows Connected.

If it still fails

  • Copy the error shown where the Gateway was started (or select Copy error details if SMTO shows it) and send it to the person who set up this Gateway. Don't keep restarting it until the value is changed; it will stop the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway settings validation rejected terminal_input_idle_seconds (GATEWAY_TERMINAL_INPUT_IDLE_SECONDS) because it is negative; zero (detection off) or a positive number of seconds is required.

What this means

  • terminal_input_idle_seconds is negative during Gateway configuration validation. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • terminal_input_idle_seconds is negative during Gateway configuration validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect GATEWAY_TERMINAL_INPUT_IDLE_SECONDS rather than the separate terminal-lifetime limit.

How to fix it

  • Set GATEWAY_TERMINAL_INPUT_IDLE_SECONDS on the Gateway host to 0 (disables waiting-for-input detection) or a positive number of seconds (default 15), or unset it, then restart the Gateway.
  • Set GATEWAY_TERMINAL_INPUT_IDLE_SECONDS to the intended nonnegative duration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A nonnegative input-idle duration passes Gateway validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
